newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel - capital gains tax plan not yet decided.
newsitem.headline: Waigel - capital gains tax plan not yet decided.

text.p: German finance minister Theo Waigel said in a magazine interview that he did not give his approval to a proposal by his coalition partner party, the CDU, to introduce capital gains tax on shares.

"The CDU proposal did not get my vote. The impact on Frankfurt as a place to do business has yet to be examined," Waigel said in an interview with the current issue of the news magazine Focus, due out next week.
Waigel is a member of the CSU, which has close links with Chancellor Helmut Kohl's CDU, the main party in the ruling coalition in Germany.
The CDU mooted the idea of taxing capital gains on securities in a policy document issued on Tuesday last as part of its overall tax reform plan.
The proposed capital gains tax is part of a planned broad tax reform aimed at lowering Germany's overall tax burden. Bonn plans to implement the reform in 1999.

Analysts contacted by Reuters last week said they feared that the proposal would stifle private investor interest just as many Germans look set to buy shares for the first time, when Deutsche Telekom is floated in November.
